name: Qatar Real Estate Verified Reference Library
curation: Official government and master developer primary sources prioritized. Time-sensitive claims require re-verification.
publication_policy: Source-verified facts are reference-only pending TAAMEER Marketing approval for branded external claims.

entries.title: Foreign ownership legal framework
entries.claim: Qatar Law No. 16 of 2018 regulates non-Qatari real estate ownership and usufruct. Designated areas and conditions are set through Cabinet decisions; the 2026 amendment should be considered when discussing current designated areas.

entries.title: Foreign freehold areas updated in 2026
entries.claim: Cabinet Decision No. 21 of 2026 amended Decision No. 28 of 2020. An updated list contains 10 designated entries, including The Pearl Island, Lusail, Al Kharayej, Jabal Thuaileb and Simaisma Resort and Beach Project. Exact plot eligibility must be verified with Ministry of Justice before advertising a unit as freehold.

entries.title: Ten 2026 designated freehold area entries
entries.claim: The updated 2026 list includes West Bay (Legtaifiya, Zone 66), The Pearl (Zone 66), Al Khor Resort (Zone 74), Dafna (Zone 60), Dafna (Zone 61), Onaiza (Zone 63), Lusail (Zone 69), Al Kharayej (Zone 69), Jabal Thuaileb (Zone 69) and Simaisma Resort and Beach Project (Zone 70). This is an area-level summary, not proof of eligibility for any specific unit.
entries.source_title: The Peninsula — Report on 2026 Gazette amendment

entries.title: Freehold versus usufruct
entries.claim: Freehold provides ownership in designated areas, while usufruct grants rights to use or lease property for up to 99 years, renewable under applicable rules. The exact legal rights must be checked against the property deed and transaction documents.

entries.title: QAR 730,000 property-linked residence category
entries.claim: Ministry of Justice guidance states that qualifying ownership of property valued at least QAR 730,000 may provide eligibility for real-estate residency without a sponsor, subject to the applicable conditions including at least 90 days' presence in Qatar each year. Residency is not automatic; applicants must satisfy the authorities' requirements.
entries.source_title: Ministry of Justice — Non-Qatari ownership and use

entries.title: QAR 3,650,000 enhanced residence benefits category
entries.claim: Ministry of Justice guidance states qualifying property valued at least QAR 3,650,000 may provide real-estate residency with certain permanent-residency-card-type benefits related to healthcare, education and investment, subject to requirements including at least 90 days in Qatar annually. It is not an automatic grant of permanent-resident status or nationality.

entries.title: Real estate residence application
entries.claim: The Ministry of Justice has a service for obtaining approval for real-estate residency in designated freehold or usufruct areas. Its listed documents include identification, title deed and, for certain non-residents, a good-conduct certificate. Eligibility, status and document requirements should be confirmed directly with the Ministry.
entries.source_title: Ministry of Justice — Obtaining Approval for Real Estate Residency

entries.title: Transfer registration fee and title documents
entries.claim: The Ministry of Justice's sale-transfer service lists a registration fee of 0.25% of the property or unit value, plus QAR 100 for a printed title deed and/or plan; exemptions may apply under Minister of Justice Decision No. 5 of 2026. Always verify transaction-specific fees before quoting a total.
entries.source_title: Ministry of Justice — Transfer of ownership by sale

entries.title: Real estate registration and title verification
entries.claim: Qatar's Ministry of Justice Real Estate Registration Department maintains registration records, processes relevant transactions and issues title deeds and certificates of rights. Buyers should verify the deed, unit status and registration directly with competent authorities.
entries.source_title: Ministry of Justice — Real Estate Registration Department

entries.title: Aqarat regulator and project licensing
entries.claim: Aqarat, Qatar's Real Estate Regulatory Authority, oversees developer and development-project licensing within its remit, seeks investor protection and publishes legislation and regulatory services. Verify a project's specific approvals before describing it as licensed or fully approved.

entries.title: Off-plan project escrow accounts
entries.claim: Aqarat describes project-specific independent escrow accounts for real-estate development, with arrangements governing disbursements and links between purchaser payments and approved construction progress. Do not claim any specific TAAMEER project has an escrow account without confirming its approval and documentation.

entries.title: Owners' association legislation 2026
entries.claim: Aqarat's legislation register lists Law No. 11 of 2026 concerning owners' associations. Specific duties, service charges and governance arrangements must be verified from the law and property-specific documentation; do not infer them from this summary.

entries.title: Official first-half 2026 transaction value
entries.claim: Aqarat reported, citing Ministry of Justice registration data, that real-estate transaction value in the first half of 2026 was QAR 10.69 billion, about 5.84% above the same period in 2025. This is total registered transaction value, not a property-price-appreciation or investment-return figure.
entries.source_title: Aqarat — Qatar Real Estate Forum announcement (2026)

entries.title: Q3 2026 rental transaction indicator
entries.claim: Aqarat's indicator page lists 35,234 rental transactions for Q3 2026. This is an official administrative transaction count and should not be represented as occupancy, yield, demand growth or property price growth.

entries.title: Educational property-investment assessment
entries.claim: A prudent property assessment considers intended use, location, comparable prices and rents supported by dated data, operating costs, vacancy and liquidity risk, financing and service charges, construction and legal risks, and ownership/residency eligibility. Gross rental yield equals annual rent divided by property price, while net cash flow also deducts applicable costs; neither is guaranteed.
entries.source_title: Invest Qatar — Real estate sector overview

entries.title: Qatar sector policy and investment context
entries.claim: Invest Qatar presents real estate as part of the country's wider investment and economic diversification landscape, citing infrastructure investments, mixed-use developments and foreign-ownership rules as important market factors. These are general context, not a prediction that any property will appreciate.

entries.title: Lusail City overall master plan
entries.claim: Lusail's official city developer describes an approximately 38 sq km planned city comprising 19 integrated districts. Residential, commercial, recreation and transport uses are planned across the city; figures are master-plan scale, not guarantees of population or demand.
entries.source_title: Lusail City — The building blocks of sustainable living

entries.title: Lusail mobility and tram network
entries.claim: Lusail's official website describes a Light Rail Transit master network, pedestrian and cycle connections and a planned water-taxi mobility system. It describes four main LRT lines over 38.5 km. Planned networks and operating services must not be conflated; verify current operational routes and stations before telling buyers a transport service is available.

entries.title: How to discuss Lusail thoughtfully
entries.claim: When filming in Lusail, discuss district-specific lifestyles, pedestrian access, commuting options, services and proximity to an individual project using verified maps. The city contains different districts with different characteristics; avoid claiming every Lusail building is waterfront or near a particular tram stop.

entries.title: The Pearl Island developer facts
entries.claim: UDC, the master developer, describes The Pearl Island as a man-made mixed-use waterfront island on approximately 4 million sq m of reclaimed land, about 350 m offshore from the West Bay district. It comprises multiple precincts with residential, retail, dining and entertainment uses.
entries.source_title: United Development Company — Projects / The Pearl Island

entries.title: The Pearl precinct identity
entries.claim: UDC describes The Pearl Island as comprising 10 architecturally distinctive precincts. Content should distinguish specific precincts and building locations rather than treating the island as a single interchangeable neighbourhood.

entries.title: The Pearl Island and foreign ownership
entries.claim: The Pearl Island appears in Qatar's designated freehold ownership areas for non-Qataris. Specific development, plot, title and transaction eligibility must still be verified; ownership is not proof of automatic residency.

entries.title: Qetaifan Island North masterplan scale
entries.claim: Qetaifan Projects, the master developer, identifies Qetaifan Island North as an approximately 1.3 million sq m island development near Lusail. The master plan includes leisure, waterfront residential, hotels, retail and recreational amenities. Specific offerings depend on individual development approvals.

entries.title: Qetaifan Island North attraction mix
entries.claim: Qetaifan Projects' master-plan website presents a waterpark, hotel, residential, retail/festival plazas, a linear park and beach-club components. Do not imply every attraction is operating or included with a particular TAAMEER unit without current independent confirmation.

entries.title: Qetaifan individual plot ownership status
entries.claim: Qetaifan Island North is part of the Lusail-area master plan, but eligibility for a non-Qatari to hold freehold title to a specific island unit must be confirmed against the current cadastral zoning, title and Ministry of Justice requirements. Do not simply assert every unit on the island is freehold.
